study type: Cross-sectional with a nested case-control study
exposure: obstetric complications (hypertensive disorders, antepartum haemorrhage, prolonged/obstructed labour)
cohort: Women giving birth to a live or stillborn baby weighing >2000 g.
finding: Of 6550 births, 10.2% had an adverse perinatal outcome, with higher rates among neonates whose mothers had antepartum haemorrhage or prolonged/obstructed labour, and emergency referral and caesarean section generally did not alter IP-NE risks except in cases of prolonged/obstructed labour.
mod_finding: Emergency caesarean section did not alter the risks of IP-NE in women with obstetric complications except for prolonged/obstructed labour, where it significantly decreased the predicted probability of IP-NE from 0.73 to 0.45.
